analysis:
Only head-side source excerpts of coordinator/api/consumer.go (lines 1-~595 and 596-~1300) were supplied, with no patch hunks, so the changed lines could not be identified. I read the visible code against T-049, T-053, T-054, TB-001, TB-002, TB-007 and the A-001 and A-009 assets and found no concrete regression.

What I checked:
- dispatchWithReserver (about lines 880-1130): the request-absolute first-content deadline check runs before reservation. Per-provider reservation top-up and refund, E2E parsing of provider.PublicKey, session-key generation and e2e.Encrypt all run before the write. The sealed body comes from bodyForCacheAttempt. All failure paths call refundExtra, cleanupPending and releaseUnsentDispatch, and add the provider to excludeProviders where applicable. A missing PublicKey fails closed with 503, so there is no plaintext fallback.
- onDispatched fires only from the writer's deferred callback after socket handoff. This matches the T-053 intent that final authorization is checked at dispatch, but the check itself lives in writeProviderInferenceRequestDeferred and the registry writer, which were not supplied.
- cancelDispatch and refundProviderExtra: refunds are guarded by the RemovePending result. refundProviderExtra returns early when ModelTokenReservationID is set, so the extra reservation is not refunded through this path. Whether that is a billing leak depends on code outside the excerpt.
- Media fetch (T-049): no media-resolution code appears in these excerpts, so there is no evidence of a regression there.
- providerBodySizeError is truncated at the end of unit 8, so its remaining logic was not reviewed.

For the next pass: review the actual diff for consumer.go, the writer's final-authorization check (registry and provider write path), and the rest of the post-line-1300 handler code.
